title: Format partitions for Arch Linux installation
summary: Create file systems on the newly created partitions. This example shows formatting a root partition as Ext4 and an EFI partition as FAT32.
prerequisites: Partitions created using fdisk or similar tool

steps.explain: Format the root partition with Ext4. Replace <ROOT_PARTITION> with the device path (e.g., /dev/sda2).

placeholders.name: ROOT_PARTITION
placeholders.description: Device path of the root partition

steps.expect: Output indicating the file system was created.

steps.explain: If you created a new EFI system partition, format it with FAT32. Replace <EFI_PARTITION> with the device path (e.g., /dev/sda1). Do NOT format if an EFI partition already exists.

placeholders.name: EFI_PARTITION
placeholders.description: Device path of the EFI system partition

steps.expect: Output indicating the FAT32 file system was created.

steps.explain: If you created a swap partition, initialize it.

placeholders.name: SWAP_PARTITION
placeholders.description: Device path of the swap partition

steps.expect: Output indicating swap space was initialized.

warnings: Formatting destroys all data on the specified partitions.
Do not format an existing EFI system partition as it may contain boot loaders for other operating systems.

rollback.explain: There is no simple rollback for formatting. You must restore data from backups or re-partition and re-format if you made a mistake.
